import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 770

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/770](https://www.erdosproblems.com/770)
 - [Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical
    Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
 - [Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal,
    Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
-/

open Set ENat Filter

namespace Erdos770


/-- Let $h n$ be the minimal number such that $2 ^ n - 1, \dots, h(n) ^ n - 1$
are collectively coprime. -/
noncomputable def h (n : ℕ) : ℕ∞ := sInf {m | 2 < m ∧
  ((Finset.Icc 2 m.toNat).image fun i => (i ^ n - 1)).gcd id = 1}

/-- `n + 1` is prime iff `h n = n + 1`. This is described as 'easy to see' in [Er74b]. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem Nat.Prime.h_eq_add_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 < n) : h n = n + 1 ↔ (n + 1).Prime := by
  sorry

/-- For odd `n`, the values of `h n` form an unbounded set.
This is described as 'easy to see' in [Er74b]. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.variants.odd_h_unbounded : Unbounded (· ≤ ·) (ENat.toNat '' (h '' Odd)):= by
  sorry


/-- For every prime `p`, does the density of integers with `h n = p` exist? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ a, HasDensity {n | h n = p} a := by
  sorry

/-- Does `liminf h n = ∞`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ liminf h atTop = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/-- Is it true that if `p` is the greatest prime such that `p - 1 ∣ n` and `p > n ^ ε`, then
`h n = p`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    let p := sSup {m : ℕ | m.Prime ∧ m - 1 ∣ n}
    p > (n : ℝ) ^ (ε : ℝ) → h n = p := by
  sorry

/-- It is probably true that `h n = 3` for infinitely many `n`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.variants.three : {n | h n = 3}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos770

findings.description: The module bibliography lists [Er49d] and [Ma66], two papers about the strong law of large numbers and Fourier-series convergence, rather than the paper containing these number-theory problems. The relevant [Er74b], cited in the two textbook theorem docstrings, is missing from the bibliography. The mathematical statements are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The source page identifies problem 770 with [Er74b]. Erdős, “Remarks on some problems in number theory,” Math. Balkanica 4 (1974), pp. 199–200, defines h(n) and states the prime characterization, odd-input unboundedness, density question, large-prime question, and conjecture about h(n)=3. See https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-27.pdf. The listed 1949 and 1966 papers instead discuss almost-everywhere convergence for lacunary sequences of functions.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace [Er49d] and [Ma66] with [Er74b]: Erdős, P., “Remarks on some problems in number theory,” Math. Balkanica 4 (1974), 197–202, linking to https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-27.pdf. Retain the problem-page reference.

reformulations.difference: The helper uses extended naturals and requires m > 2. It therefore has h(0)=∞ and h(1)=3; interpreting the ordinary least-index definition as permitting a singleton gives h(1)=2 instead.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Allowing m=2 changes nothing for n≥2, since the singleton gcd is 2^n−1≥3. All positive inputs have finite h. The prime characterization is restricted to n>2, and its omitted positive boundary cases are elementary with the ordinary convention. Every other statement is unchanged by the finite boundary modification: natural density, infinitude, unboundedness of natural-valued images, liminf, and eventual assertions. Scratch proofs establish agreement for n≥2, the prime-characterization domain equivalence, and the infinitude and liminf equivalences; density invariance under finite changes was checked mathematically rather than formalized.

reformulations.difference: Unboundedness is expressed after applying ENat.toNat to the values of h on odd inputs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every odd natural is positive, and h(n)<∞ for every positive n. Consequently toNat never encounters its exceptional infinity-to-zero case on this image. The statement is equivalent to ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, Odd n ∧ (B : ℕ∞) < h n. This exact equivalence was proved in the scratch file without using admitted problem theorems.

reformulations.difference: Lean makes the asymptotic quantifiers explicit and represents the greatest prime by a natural-number supremum, without separately excluding n=0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source discussion explicitly interprets the question for each fixed ε>0 and sufficiently large n, with the threshold depending on ε. For n>0, the prime set contains 2, and p−1∣n implies p≤n+1, so its supremum is its genuine greatest element. At n=0 the set is unbounded and Nat.sSup returns 0, but this single input is immaterial under the eventual quantifier. An equivalence replacing the supremum formulation by an explicitly quantified IsGreatest prime was proved in Lean.

review.notes: Checked the definition and all six theorems; no substantive mathematical misformalization found. In particular, the exact website LaTeX asks “Does liminf h(n)=∞?”, so parts.ii is faithful despite the separate conjecture that h(n)=3 infinitely often. The source remains OPEN; its July 2026 partial-proof notice explicitly leaves the density, liminf, and general-ε questions unresolved. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully and contains independent boundary, finiteness, and equivalence proofs, plus finite gcd computations. These proofs do not rely on the file's admitted theorems. The reviewed file was not modified.
